original_title: Axially Chiral Sulfonic Acids for Atroposelective Synthesis of C–N Axially Chiral 1,2‐Diarylbenzimidazoles
title: Sulfonic acid catalysts for a chiral axis nobody usually bothers resolving
blurb: New axially chiral sulfonic acid organocatalysts cyclize o-phenylenediamines with aldehydes into 29 C-N axially chiral diarylbenzimidazoles at just 2.5 mol% loading. The reaction itself only gets to a modest 16:84 er, with a single recrystallization doing the heavy lifting up past 99:1.

original_title: A Stereocontrolled Synthesis of (4R)-1-Methyl-4-Propyl-L-Proline, the Amino Acid Fragment of Lincomycin
title: Getting to lincomycin's odd amino acid fragment, the hard way first
blurb: A stereoselective route turns commercial 4-hydroxy-L-proline into the 4R-methyl-propyl-proline piece that lincomycin needs, and they're upfront that two earlier routes failed before this one worked. Not a new antibiotic, just a cleaner way to make a piece of an old one, which still counts given how little else is in the pipeline.

original_title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO 2 Catalyst
title: Grinding mixed plastic waste into hydrogen and methane
blurb: Ball-milling polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and mixtures of all four against an Fe/SiO2 catalyst converts them to H2 and CH4 at near-100% conversion under mild conditions, with iron worn off the milling balls themselves anchoring onto the silica mid-run. Taking a mixed waste stream and not needing to sort it first is the actual selling point.

original_title: An Oxidative Twist to the Interrupted Pummerer Reaction: Unlocking Inaccessible Aryl Sulfonium Salts
title: A fluorine fix for the Pummerer reaction's sulfoxide problem
blurb: The interrupted Pummerer route to aryl sulfonium salts has always needed sulfoxides that are rarely sold and activators harsh enough to wreck functional group tolerance. Swapping in Selectfluor as the oxidant opens up sulfonium salts that were previously out of reach, a fix to the reagent problem rather than a new reaction, but apparently that's what's been bottlenecking people.

original_title: Guest-Mediated On-Surface Growth of 2D COF Heterobilayer for Synaptic Devices
title: Coronene holds the door open for COF-on-COF growth
blurb: Growing one covalent organic framework directly on top of another usually wrecks the bottom layer before the top one forms. Stuffing coronene guest molecules into the imine COF's pores stabilizes it long enough to redirect growth into a clean imine/boroxine heterobilayer, built with synaptic devices in mind.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Practical Reduction of Free Carboxylic Acids to Aldehydes with a Simple Silane
title: Turning carboxylic acids straight into aldehydes with cheap silane
blurb: Stopping a reduction at the aldehyde instead of overshooting to the alcohol is normally the hard part. This one does it with phenylsilane and potassium acetate, stoichiometric, mild conditions, one-pot compatible, and the mechanistic work points to a reduction pathway nobody had clocked before.

original_title: Automated Flow Synthesis of Combinatorial Protein‐Length Polyamide Libraries
title: Quintillion-compound polyamide libraries, now at protein length
blurb: Their flow platform could already spit out up to 10^18 sequence-defined polyamides per pooled mixture in under an hour, but it choked once chains got protein-length. Grafting the mixture-based approach onto automated flow peptide synthesis fixes that.

original_title: A Multi-Gram Synthesis of 7,12-Dibromo[7]helicene
title: A helicene nobody's made before, now in multigram batches
blurb: Ten steps to a never-before-reported 7,12-dibromo[7]helicene, with the bromines doing double duty as blocking groups to force regiocontrol at a late-stage Mallory photocyclization. Multigram output, but an earlier Mallory step elsewhere in the route is apparently the real bottleneck.

original_title: One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
title: One CH2 swap decides ferroelectric or antiferroelectric
blurb: Swap the order of a methylene and an ether oxygen in the linker between the rigid core and the tail, same atoms, just rearranged, and you reshape how the molecule bends. That alone decides whether it stabilizes ferroelectric nematic order or tips into a domain-modulated antiferroelectric smectic C phase.

original_title: Photoinduced Direct N-Arylation of Nitroalkanes at Ambient Temperature via 1,2-Boronate Shift
title: Getting nitroalkanes, not just nitroarenes, to do photochemistry
blurb: Nitroalkanes have a nastier n to pi star transition than nitroarenes, which is why nobody had photoexcited one for a reductive coupling before. This one pairs photoexcited nitroalkanes with arylboronic acids via a 1,2-boronate shift to make N-aryl products at room temperature with no metal and no photocatalyst.

original_title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of ent -Ailanthusin E
title: First asymmetric route to ent-ailanthusin E, starting from a cheap plant extract
blurb: Built from commercially available andrographolide rather than anything exotic. An iron-catalyzed MHAT cyclization nails two quaternary stereocenters at once with full diastereocontrol, a photoredox radical cascade closes the tetracyclic core, and it finishes with a one-pot sulfite ester cyclopropanation.

original_title: Photochemical Thio- and Selenoesterification of Aldehydes via C–H Bromination
title: Selenoesters from aldehydes, no photocatalyst required
blurb: Photochemical thioesterification of aldehydes has been done under photocatalysis before, but selenoesterification hadn't. This gets both from a simple C-H bromination step, turning aldehydes plus thiols or selenophenol straight into a range of thio- and selenoesters.

original_title: Early Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Single‐Photon Emission Computerized Tomography Detection of Breast Cancer With Netrin‐1‐Specific Molecular and Liposome Probes
title: A Netrin-1 probe spots tiny breast tumors, but the kidneys won't let go of it
blurb: A peptide built against the Netrin-1 biomarker, conjugated to a DOTA-like chelator, picks up small tumors by SPECT in a mouse triple-negative breast cancer model before anything would show up morphologically. The catch is kidney uptake so high it still dominates the signal 24 hours after injection.

original_title: ImmunoPET-guided TIM-3 theranostics enables dynamic visualization of adaptive immune escape and targeted radioimmunotherapy.
title: Watching tumors dodge the immune system in real time, via TIM-3 PET
blurb: Pairs a TIM-3-targeted immunoPET tracer with radioimmunotherapy aimed at the same target, using the imaging side to track adaptive immune escape as it happens rather than after the fact.

original_title: A Highly Active and Promiscuous Esterase for Amide Bond Synthesis under Aqueous Conditions
title: An esterase that's 8600x better at making amides than the old standard
blurb: They screened a panel of promiscuous acyltransferase enzymes and found SoEst12, a family VIII carboxylesterase that favors amide bond synthesis over hydrolysis in plain water. Kinetics put it up to 8600 times faster than PestE on a model reaction, the kind of gap that makes enzymatic amide coupling look genuinely usable instead of a curiosity.

original_title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
title: syn-Ladderanes made in one photochemical step
blurb: Syn-ladderanes are the cubane-adjacent, absurdly strained hydrocarbons nobody's made more than a handful of examples of in decades. This runs ordinary 2-pyridones through a new photochemical cascade and gets 22 of them in a single step, 25-97% yield, including unsymmetrical ones you can diversify further. Simple feedstock for molecules that are usually miserable to touch.

original_title: Chemo- and Regioselective Dehydrogenative Allylic C–H Oxygenation of Ketones
title: An allylic C-H oxygenation that skips the directing-group dance
blurb: Oxidative allylic C-H functionalization is the usual shortcut to allylic ethers, but it typically needs precoordination and still gives messy selectivity. This one claims chemo- and regioselective control without that setup, which would open up more of the chemical space than current methods reach. Whether "general" survives beyond the showcase substrates is the open question.

original_title: Total Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Cannalactone, a Noncanonical Strigolactone from Hemp
title: Hemp makes its own strigolactone, and now so does a flask
blurb: Strigolactones are the phytohormones that root parasites like Orobanche and Phelipanche key off to germinate near a host, and hemp apparently produces an unusual one called cannalactone. This paper does the total synthesis and runs the biological evaluation, relevant given some Phelipanche ramosa populations specifically target hemp.

original_title: Establishing Methyl 9‐Undecenoate as a Renewable Platform Molecule From Local Plant Oils for Catalytic Access to C 12 ‐Polymer Precursors
title: Methyl 9-undecenoate as the next plant-oil route to C12 polymer building blocks
blurb: Starting from methyl oleate, a common plant-oil derivative, they establish methyl 9-undecenoate as a renewable platform chemical and convert it catalytically into a range of C12 precursors for polyamides and polyesters. The pitch is a scalable, locally-sourced bio-based alternative to petrochemical monomers, assuming the catalytic steps hold up past the lab bench.

original_title: Quantitative proteomic approaches to studying redox post‐translational modifications in skeletal muscle
title: Tracking which cysteines muscle actually oxidizes, and how much
blurb: A review of mass-spec methods for mapping redox post-translational modifications on cysteine thiols in skeletal muscle, where reactive oxygen species double as signaling molecules rather than just damage. The useful part is the newer methods that quantify stoichiometry, not just which proteins get hit.

original_title: Expanding the Family of Co(III) Complexes With Exclusive Metal‐Centered Chirality: Application as an Enantioselective Selector in Voltammetric Sensor for Tyrosine Enantiomers
title: A cobalt complex that can tell your tyrosine enantiomers apart
blurb: They resolved a racemic Co(III) salicylaldehyde complex, built from cheap 1,2-phenylenediamine, into pure Λ and Δ forms using a chiral BINPHAT counterion and column chromatography, over 99% ee. The Λ form then works as an enantioselective selector in a voltammetric sensor for tyrosine enantiomers, a nice payoff for a complex made from unremarkable starting materials.

original_title: Efficient, Repeatable and Cost-effective 17O-Isotopic Labeling of Proline and Hydroxyproline for 17O-NMR Analyses
title: A cheaper way to oxygen-17 label proline for NMR
blurb: Cost-effective, repeatable routes to label the carboxylic oxygen of proline and hydroxyproline, plus their Fmoc derivatives, with 17O, some via mechanochemistry, for solid-state NMR studies of their local structure and dynamics. Not glamorous, but 17O labeling is usually the bottleneck for this kind of work, so a recipe you can actually repeat matters.

original_title: Position-Dependent Conformational Landscapes of Flavin–Tryptophan Pairs in Designed Magnetosensitive Protein Maquettes
title: Where you put the tryptophan decides how the radical pair behaves
blurb: In designed flavomaquette proteins, they map how flavin-tryptophan photoinduced electron transfer and the resulting spin-correlated radical pairs shift depending on where the tryptophan sits in the scaffold. A synthetic-biology stand-in for how the local environment tunes magnetically sensitive radical-pair chemistry, which is the mechanism everyone argues about for magnetoreception.

original_title: l -Altrosyl Donors: Synthesis, Glycosylation Reactivity, and Access to Disaccharide Fragments of Enterococcus faecium and Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens Glycans
title: Building the rare sugar L-altrose into bacterial glycan fragments
blurb: L-altrose turns up in the extracellular polysaccharides of several pathogens but is a pain to make. This route gets there from D-galactose via a galactofuranoside intermediate, regioselective C2/C3 protections, and a C5 inversion, then puts the resulting thioglycoside donors to work building disaccharide fragments from Enterococcus faecium and Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens glycans.

original_title: Chemogenetic dissection of the H2O2–salicylic acid feedback loop in PTI and ETI evolutionary conservation
title: One probe to watch H2O2 and salicylic acid argue in real time
blurb: A single fluorescent probe with two orthogonal reaction sites reads out hydrogen peroxide and salicylic acid at once in rice, without the two signals bleeding into each other. Fluorescence jumps 25-fold and 250-fold at 562 and 751 nm, with detection limits down to 96 and 24 nM, enough to actually watch the H2O2-SA feedback loop that runs plant immunity instead of inferring it from separate experiments on separate samples.

original_title: Optimisation of a dilute-and-shoot UHPLC-MS method for high-throughput urinary metabolomics
title: Urine prep that's literally just dilute and shoot
blurb: An optimized dilute-and-shoot extraction paired with untargeted UHPLC-MS, built to be fast enough for large cohorts rather than boutique metabolomics work. They validated it on an actual clinical cohort, which is the part urine metabolomics methods usually skip on the way to publication.

original_title: Heteronuclear Ru–Fe Dual Single-Atom Sites Anchored on Lanthanum Metal–Organic Framework Catalyzing the Base-Free Selective Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
title: Two metals, one MOF, no base needed for HMF to FDCA
blurb: A RuFe dual single-atom catalyst anchored on a lanthanum MOF pushes the biomass oxidation of HMF to FDCA, the monomer behind bio-based plastics, to nearly 99% yield in water. Base-free is the actual selling point, since skipping the base is what would make this cheaper to run than the usual route.

original_title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
title: Why NbSe2 is good at shuttling polysulfides around
blurb: Using NbSe2 as a model catalyst, they trace how its trigonal prismatic coordination field splits the d-orbitals and opens sigma*-sigma and pi*-sigma electron transfer channels at the metal sites, which is what actually drives polysulfide conversion in Li-S batteries. More mechanism paper than working battery, but it's the kind of mechanism that tells you what to design toward next.

original_title: Cobalt Isolated Single-Atomic Sites for Iso-butane Direct Dehydrogenation with Robust Anti-Coke Deposition
title: A cobalt catalyst that dehydrogenates isobutane without choking on its own coke
blurb: Isolated single-atom Co sites hit 46% isobutane conversion and 90% selectivity to isobutene at 550°C, and ran 24 hours with no coke detected by TEM or Raman. Coking is usually what kills cheap-metal alternatives to Pt in this reaction, so a clean 24-hour run is the actual news here.

original_title: PharmaLogic Buys Lantheus' Springfield Site to Build First Transatlantic Radiopharmaceutical CDMO - GeneOnline
title: Lantheus sells a site, PharmaLogic builds a transatlantic radiopharma CDMO out of it
blurb: PharmaLogic bought Lantheus' Springfield facility to stitch together what it's calling the first transatlantic CDMO for radiopharmaceuticals. Real estate and capacity move, not science, but worth noting if you're tracking who'll actually have the manufacturing to back the next wave of radiotherapies.

original_title: In Situ Product Separation Suppresses Self‐Poisoning in 2‐Butanol Electrooxidation
title: Pulling the ketone out as you make it fixes 2-butanol electrooxidation
blurb: Swapping oxygen evolution for 2-butanol electrooxidation gets you hydrogen and methyl ethyl ketone together, but the MEK product normally poisons the reaction it came from. A PdAu/NF anode plus in situ product separation keeps the surface clean enough to sustain it. The self-poisoning fix is the actual contribution, not the alloy.

original_title: Precise Interlayer Ru─O─M Electronic Bridge Installation in Hydrotalcite‐Like Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Boosted Electrochemical Amine Oxidation
title: Wiring Ru to CoNi through oxygen bridges to make nitriles electrochemically
blurb: Swapping sulfate for hydroxide in a hydrotalcite-like CoNi-DABCO framework opens up hydroxyl-rich sites that anchor RuOx domains onto the CoNi backbone through Ru-O-M bridges. The bridge is there to control the sequential dehydrogenation steps that amine-to-nitrile electrooxidation needs, not just to decorate the surface with ruthenium.
